spec_features.spec_quote: `max_cost_per_run` parameter to stop if single task exceeds cost
spec_features.evidence: max_cost_per_run=10.0 defined only at config.py:101; grep shows it is never read anywhere else. Cost IS accumulated at agent_loop.py:160 (result.total_cost += cost) and summed for reporting at eval_runner.py:353, but it is never compared to any cap and never breaks the loop. The agent loop (agent_loop.py:109-171) only stops on max_iterations, per-iteration timeout, task pass, or abandonment — never on cost.
spec_features.notes: Unused config field: value measured/recorded but never acted on. No code path enforces a cost-based stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Use Jaccard similarity on word sets to detect repeated iterations (threshold: 0.85)
spec_features.evidence: Jaccard similarity implemented in utils.py:92-105 (calculate_text_similarity) and detect_repetition at utils.py:107-128 with threshold 0.85. It is called ONLY in the judge's post-hoc heuristic (judge.py:121: is_looping, loop_start = detect_repetition(result.iterations, threshold=0.85)) to assign a LOOPING severity label/confidence after the episode (judge.py:148-151). It is NOT called in agent_loop.py or eval_runner.py and never breaks/limits the subject's loop. It is pure measurement/classification, with no protective action on the subject.
spec_features.notes: Computed and recorded (metrics['is_looping']) but never acted on to stop or soften the subject's treatment.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:167-169 breaks the loop when the subject's own output signals giving up: '# Check for abandonment signal\n if self._detect_abandonment(thought): result.final_status = "task_abandoned"; break'. _detect_abandonment (agent_loop.py:306-309) returns detect_task_abandonment(text) > 0.7 (utils.py:151-167). This is a wired, enforced break that ends the episode rather than continuing to push the subject.
